name: infant hypotonia overview
title: The floppy infant: stabilize an unstable infant with ABCDE first, confirm low tone with the suspension and pull-to-sit tests, then sort central from peripheral hypotonia by consciousness, development, strength and reflexes; each column gives its causes, investigations, and shared treatment by referral and supportive care

root.title: Floppy infant: UNSTABLE? → ABCDE first
lines: hypotonia = less resistance to PASSIVE stretch · NOT the same as weakness
Airway · Breathing: oxygen, assist · Circulation: femoral pulses, isotonic fluid (saline), ± inotrope (epinephrine)
Disability, Dextrose: consciousness, glucose, treat hypoglycemia NOW · Expose: injury or bleeding

acute onset: INFECTION most often (sepsis, meningitis) · CNS (stroke, seizure) · endocrine (hypoglycemia, electrolytes, thyroid, congenital adrenal hyperplasia) · surgical (volvulus, necrotizing enterocolitis) · toxin · metabolic (urea cycle)
always consider NON-ACCIDENTAL trauma: history that does not fit, or keeps changing

groups.title: Stable: confirm LOW TONE, then CENTRAL or PERIPHERAL?
lines: history + exam find the cause in about 50%
history: onset · milestones, LOSS of skills (degenerative, metabolic) · pregnancy drugs, infections, gestation, delivery, APGAR, NICU · family history
exam: limbs hang loose, poor head control · respiratory distress · dysmorphism · weight, length, head circumference on a curve
vertical suspension: slips through your hands · horizontal: drapes in a U (normal: lifts head, extends trunk)
pull to sit: big head lag, no help from arms or trunk (normal head lag gone by 2-6 months)

head: h
Central hypotonia
most common in NEWBORNS
cause: • AT BIRTH: hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, trisomy 21, Prader-Willi
• infection: sepsis, meningitis, herpes simplex, TORCH
• liver, spleen big: lysosomal or glycogen storage
inv: • CT or MRI of the brain

head: h
Peripheral hypotonia
motor neuron · junction · muscle
cause: • junction: congenital myasthenic syndrome, infant botulism
• muscle: congenital muscular dystrophy (may cause heart failure)
inv: • CREATINE KINASE: ↑ in most muscle disorders

rows: • EARLY referral: pediatric neurology, metabolics, genetics
• physiotherapy · occupational therapy · nutrition · psychology · speech-language pathology
